mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession (UNRATE < 2%).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing market (HOUST) indicates a consumption-led slowdown with offsetting housing strength, resulting in flat-to-positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as sector rotation occurs.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
regime_hint: late-cycle consumption deceleration with housing resilience
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or sector rotation into housing does not materialize (HOUST underperforms market).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes Fed tightening and increased input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the Fed does not raise rates within the subsequent quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average, combined with rising real savings (RSAFS), indicates supply-side weakness with elevated precautionary savings, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days due to lower earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months AND RSAFS > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong demand growth (GDPC1 > 3% YoY).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in CPIAUCSL above 4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 3% signals a lagged inflation response to loose policy, which typically precedes a hawkish Fed pivot and higher real yields, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% AND FEDFUNDS < 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the Fed does not raise rates within the next FOMC meeting.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll growth acceleration (PAYEMS) above 300k for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which typically supports corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or earnings growth disappoints despite strong payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% YoY indicates a broad-based demand contraction, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to reduced consumer and construction sector earnings.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -1% AND HOUST YoY change < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the decline is reversed within one quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the federal funds rate below 2% for four consecutive months signals an extended easing cycle, which reduces required equity risk premiums and supports higher valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days under stable inflation conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for 4 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL change < 0.2% monthly
regime_hint: prolonged monetary easing with stable inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation accelerates (CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY) during the period.
